name: CCFR
summary: CCFR used a massive iron calorimeter and muon spectrometer at Fermilab to measure high-energy neutrino-nucleon scattering, electroweak parameters, nucleon structure and oscillation limits.
physics_targets: Charm, strange-quark content and short-baseline oscillations
detection_principle: Iron target plates interleaved with scintillation counters and tracking chambers sampled hadronic showers, while a downstream magnetized spectrometer measured outgoing muons. Event length separated predominantly neutral-current samples from charged-current muon events.

status.label: Completed / historical

key_parameters.value: 30-500 GeV, mean about 140 GeV in the cited analysis

results.summary: Used longitudinal energy-deposition differences to constrain electron- and tau-flavour appearance at high mass-squared splittings.

science_scope: The record describes the named experiment as one programme; detector subsystems and repeated analyses are not counted as independent experiments.

media.caption: The upgraded NuTeV layout of the iron-calorimeter and muon-spectrometer apparatus descended from CCFR; electronics and beam conditions differ between the two programmes.
